deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared error-recovery scenario passes with screen reader, magnification, voice control, and keyboard-only input.

controls.reason: Cross-matrix tests are objective, but representative critical journeys and supported browser, device, and assistive-technology scope require contextual selection.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared critical journey has current results for every cell in the approved support matrix.

controls.reason: Screen-reader/browser matrix coverage is measurable, but multiple major and appropriate combinations depend on the user population and market.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved test matrix contains at least two declared major screen-reader and browser combinations with current results.

controls.reason: Capability test evidence is objective, but applicability to the supported population requires accessibility and product judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared applicable magnification, zoom, reflow, voice, switch, caption, and platform-setting mode has current results.

controls.reason: Orientation-lock behavior is detectable, but whether a specific orientation is essential requires task and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every orientation-locked surface has an approved essential-orientation exception; all others operate in supported orientations.

controls.reason: Supported mobile layout conditions provide exact geometry assertions for control and instruction visibility.

deterministic_clauses.statement: No virtual keyboard, safe area, cutout, or magnification state covers declared controls or instructions in the supported matrix.

controls.reason: Accessibility and visual orders can be extracted, but whether they match the intended task order requires semantic interaction judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Mobile accessibility-tree traversal order matches the declared visual-order identifiers for each tested task.

controls.reason: Applying broad WCAG principles and platform guidance to native and hybrid applications requires qualified accessibility interpretation and platform context.
Offline, cached, and installed modes are finite runtime states whose accessibility assertions can be compared with the online baseline.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared offline, cached, and installed experience passes its bound accessibility test suite.

controls.reason: Operability assertions can be tested, but understandability of notifications, deep links, shares, widgets, and dialogs requires user and content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared system-integration surface passes its supported input and programmatic-name, role, state, and focus assertions.

controls.reason: Document validators provide bounded evidence, but applicable standards and complete accessibility for diverse PDF, office, email, and downloads require specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every downloadable document passes the validator for its selected applicable document standard.

controls.reason: Document accessibility structures can be compared before and after generation or conversion using exact tagged-document assertions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Generation and conversion preserve tags, headings, reading order, bookmarks, language, alternate text, tables, links, and form semantics.

controls.reason: OCR and structural fields are inspectable, but accuracy, remediation sufficiency, and when accessible text is required need human and legal accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scanned-image document marked accessible-text-required has OCR output and structural-remediation evidence.

controls.reason: Alternative artifact and route behavior are testable, but whether a format fails user needs and an alternative is equivalent require user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every document marked unable-to-meet-needs has a reachable accessible HTML or equivalent alternative.

controls.reason: Print and export differences are mechanically detectable, but essential information and overall accessibility require semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Print and export outputs preserve every item marked essential and pass their declared accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: Upgrade events and the bound assistive-technology suite permit direct regression comparison after each component, browser, platform, or generator change.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every recorded relevant upgrade has a later successful assistive-technology regression result.

controls.reason: Unsupported-combination records and alternatives are observable, but whether an alternative is workable requires user and task judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every unsupported combination is documented and links to a tested alternative route.

controls.reason: Product-role declarations and guidance references are checkable, but whether UAAG guidance applies and how to use informative provisions require specialist interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product declared a user agent has a UAAG 2.0 applicability and guidance-use record.

controls.reason: Perceivability, operability, understandability, and assistive compatibility of the whole user-agent interface require broad empirical evaluation without a fixed protocol.
Supported accessibility APIs expose finite object properties that can be inspected for each declared user-agent surface.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Rendered content, controls, selection, focus, caret, viewport, playback, status, and document structure expose their declared accessibility API values.

controls.reason: Versioned accessibility-tree snapshots allow exact comparison through rendering, transformation, reader mode, translation, annotation, and export.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared transformation preserves expected content roles, names, relationships, order, and accessibility metadata.

controls.reason: Presentation controls are testable, but platform-role permission and the complete set of relevant presentation characteristics require product and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every presentation characteristic declared platform-permitted has a tested user control.

controls.reason: The named user-agent functions and alternative-input actions form a finite interaction matrix with exact outcomes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Browser chrome, media, document navigation, extensions, permissions, downloads, history, and settings pass the approved keyboard and alternative-input tests.

controls.reason: Navigation targets and keyboard behavior are testable, but determining which meaningful structures are present requires semantic content interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every structure type declared present exposes a tested navigation command and destination.

controls.reason: Accessible communication of security and permission messages requires comprehension and interaction evaluation without defined users, tasks, or thresholds.
Extension permissions and data flows are queryable, but excessive privilege and informed user control require security, privacy, and usability judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility extension declares permissions and data flows and exposes versioned user controls for browsing and content data.

controls.reason: Integrated test evidence is objective, but sufficient host, content, accessibility-tree, focus, keyboard, zoom, and assistive coverage requires contextual scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every embedded viewer has current integrated results covering the declared host, content, tree, focus, keyboard, zoom, and assistive-technology matrix.

controls.reason: Fallback existence and route behavior are testable, but critical user needs and whether an alternate application is accessible and adequate require user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required format or user agent marked unable to meet critical needs has a tested fallback or alternate application.

controls.reason: Detected compatibility regressions and issue types are structured facts, so policy can require every regression to be filed as a product defect.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every user-agent or assistive-technology regression has a product-defect record regardless of underlying content-change status.

controls.reason: Authoring capability and an ATAG record are observable, but determining applicability and correct use of ATAG 2.0 requires accessibility interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product declared capable of creating or editing digital content has an ATAG 2.0 applicability and evaluation record.

controls.reason: Accessibility of the whole authoring interface for authors with disabilities requires broad user and assistive-technology evaluation without a fixed protocol.
Output and transformation tests are objective, but accessible by default and complete preservation of meaningful accessibility information require semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Default generation and every declared editing, import, export, copy, and transformation path pass the approved accessibility-structure checks.

controls.reason: Missing required accessibility metadata has exact schema predicates, and prompt appearance can be exercised for each authoring action.

deterministic_clauses.statement: When required alternate text, labels, headings, captions, language, table headers, or metadata is missing, the authoring tool presents its declared prompt.

controls.reason: Correctness of author-supplied accessibility data and lower quality of a generated replacement are semantic content judgments.
Template, example, validator, suggestion, and preview presence is objective, but whether each is accessible and useful requires broader evaluation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authoring tool provides versioned templates, examples, validators, repair suggestions, and preview features with declared accessibility checks.

controls.reason: Discoverability and normal-workflow integration of accessibility checking are author usability outcomes without defined tasks, users, or thresholds.
Component contracts and acceptance suites are bounded artifacts that can be checked for explicit accessibility requirements and tests.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every design-system component contract contains accessibility requirements linked to acceptance tests.

controls.reason: The six component documentation categories are exact required fields for every shared component.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every shared component documents keyboard behavior, semantics, states, content constraints, and known limitations.

controls.reason: Selected accessibility thresholds and exception records allow design-token values to be rejected before they permit inaccessible states.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every contrast, focus, motion, spacing, and target-size token is within the approved accessibility constraints.
Any out-of-constraint token requires an explicit authenticated reviewed exception.

controls.reason: Review records and change diffs are objective, but materiality and reviewer qualification require accessibility governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every new component and every component change marked material has a pre-merge accessibility review record.

controls.reason: Accessibility behavior versions and consumer communication events are exact component-release metadata.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every component release versions accessibility behavior and every declared breaking change has authenticated consumer communication evidence.

controls.reason: Adoption timestamps and evaluation records can be checked, but sufficient evaluation of diverse third-party experiences requires contextual accessibility review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared third-party widget or flow has an accessibility evaluation dated before adoption.

controls.reason: Contract clauses are observable, but critical barriers, timely remediation, and adequate alternatives require legal, accessibility, and procurement judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable supplier contract requires remediation deadlines or an accessible alternative for barriers classified critical.

controls.reason: Inaccessible supplier components are a finite register that can require a replacement or isolation plan.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supplier component marked inaccessible links to a versioned replacement or isolation plan.

controls.reason: Conformance artifacts can be versioned and scoped, but whether vendor information is evidence-based rather than marketing and substantively current requires review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendor accessibility claim links to a dated scoped conformance artifact and supporting evidence.

controls.reason: Integrated production tests are objective, but proving the deployed experience accessible requires complete user, task, and assistive-technology scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supplier component has current integrated-product accessibility test results bound to the deployed version.

controls.reason: Procurement scoring inputs can be inspected to require actual task-accessibility results in addition to any conformance report.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility procurement score includes deployed task-accessibility evidence and is not computed solely from conformance-report presence.

controls.reason: Repeatable detector configurations and their CI coverage can be enumerated across components, templates, pages, documents, and critical flows.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Automated accessibility checks run for each declared repeatable defect class and applicable artifact or flow.

controls.reason: Tool versions, rule coverage, and false-positive or false-negative measures are exact automation-governance fields.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every automated accessibility run records tool version and rule coverage, and the program tracks false positives and false negatives.

controls.reason: The named manual test areas are a finite script-library coverage set.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The manual test library contains current scripts for keyboard, focus, zoom, text spacing, screen readers, forms, media, and cognitive access.

controls.reason: Test assertions are inspectable, but where they are reliable and applicable depends on component and tool behavior.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test layer marked accessibility-assertion-reliable contains active accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: Change triggers and review records can be matched, but material structure or dependency changes require accessibility impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying content, interaction, navigation, token, document, or dependency change links to a later accessibility review.

controls.reason: Production monitor coverage is queryable, but where monitoring is feasible and sufficient depends on platform and defect detectability.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every defect class declared production-monitorable has an active monitor for names, structure, contrast, dialogs, skip links, or document generation.

controls.reason: Feedback form fields and submission behavior can prove that diagnosis disclosure is not required.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The accessibility feedback route accepts a report without a diagnosis field or diagnosis-dependent validation.

controls.reason: Actual task impact and affected-user severity require accessibility triage judgment beyond automated issue labels.
Alternative availability is testable, but materiality and whether a temporary path is equivalently accessible require accountable user-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every defect marked material and open has a tested temporary alternative path.

controls.reason: Defect records identify the exposing input mode or assistive technology, allowing exact retest-environment matching.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every fixed defect has a successful retest using the same input mode or assistive technology recorded on the original report.

controls.reason: Recognizing recurrence, selecting systemic root causes, and choosing component, process, training, or governance fixes require human analysis.
The accessibility backlog has a finite exact required field schema and closure-evidence reference.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility defect records owner, impact, affected surfaces, workaround, target date, and closure evidence when closed.

controls.reason: Incident and review links are objective, but deciding that users lost access to an essential function requires user-impact and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility event marked essential-access-loss has operational incident and post-incident review records.

controls.reason: A third-party version inventory and accessibility baselines permit exact change-triggered regression monitoring.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every monitored third-party version change runs the bound accessibility regression suite and records its result.

controls.reason: Scope and limitation diffs can trigger exact review requirements for statements and conformance reports.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every recorded scope or known-limitation change links to a later accessibility-statement and conformance-report review.

controls.reason: Measurements can be calculated, but critical tasks and meaningful barrier events require user and accessibility context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The accessibility metrics include task-success rates and barrier frequency for every task declared critical.

controls.reason: Proving that hard pages, states, users, or technologies were not intentionally or silently excluded from metrics requires complete scope knowledge and intent analysis.
Retention fields are queryable, but sufficient evidence for internal, procurement, customer, and regulatory review depends on obligations and review purpose.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Accessibility evaluation evidence has explicit retention and access settings for each declared review audience.

controls.reason: Legitimate content, usefulness, and ranking manipulation are semantic and ethical search-governance concepts requiring human judgment.
Current official policies and technical results are observable, but which search-engine requirements and guidance are applicable requires search and regional context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every engine in the approved applicability register has current technical, spam-policy, and webmaster-guidance compliance evidence.

controls.reason: People-first value, low-value pages, doorway schemes, and hidden content are semantic editorial and search-policy judgments.
Configured claim text can be scanned, but promises and their practical meaning across ranking, indexing, traffic, rich results, and AI inclusion require semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Published search-performance claims are flagged when they use an approved prohibited guarantee pattern.

controls.reason: Proving search optimization never reduces accessibility, privacy, security, performance, or accuracy is a broad cross-quality causal claim.
The six SEO governance domains form a finite owner matrix with exact-one identity checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Technical SEO, editorial quality, structured data, international targeting, migrations, and monitoring each have one accountable owner.

controls.reason: The requirement is to document the selected external discovery services, so a versioned applicability inventory decides it exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The search applicability record lists engines, regional services, vertical products, and AI or content crawlers that matter to the product.

controls.reason: The five crawler-governance topics are explicit required policy sections.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The crawler policy covers access, content licensing, training use, archival access, and high-volume automated retrieval.

controls.reason: Policy text and public access tests can verify that crawler directives are not treated as authentication for confidential assets.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Security documentation distinguishes crawler directives from authentication and authorization.
Every confidential asset in the approved inventory requires access control independently of crawler directives.

controls.reason: Search-visible fields can be compared with page data, but accuracy and semantic reflection of identity, ratings, and availability require editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each search-visible title, description, snippet, date, price, availability, rating, and identity field links to the page source value and freshness result.

controls.reason: Crawler-user response diffs are measurable, but material misleadingness across experiments, personalization, consent, and geolocation requires semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared variant has crawler and user response snapshots with a computed content difference.

controls.reason: Deception and material difference between crawler and user content are semantic intent and impact judgments, not just byte differences.
Disclosure markers and link attributes are inspectable, but when disclosure is required and editorial controls are appropriate require legal and editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item marked sponsored, affiliate, user-generated, or automated has its declared disclosure and link attributes.

controls.reason: Evidence links are objective, but factual support and sufficiency for medical, legal, financial, safety, and other high-impact claims require domain specialists.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every claim marked factual or high-impact links to current source evidence and review metadata.

controls.reason: Using diagnostic tools without substituting their score for official guidance or product judgment concerns decision practice and accountable interpretation.
External policy change and review timestamps are observable, but major changes and material search decisions require search-governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every policy change marked major links to a later search-practice review and recorded decisions.

controls.reason: An intended-public URL inventory and crawl graph permit exact reachability checks through stable links or declared discovery mechanisms.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every intended public page is reachable from its approved discovery seed through stable crawlable links or its declared discovery mechanism.

controls.reason: HTTP success and indexing directives are objective, but whether rendered indexable content is usable requires content and crawler interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every intended indexable page returns its declared success status and exposes retrievable indexable content in the crawler test.

controls.reason: Private-page classifications and unauthenticated access probes make access-control presence directly decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every page classified private rejects unauthenticated public-network requests and requires the declared access control.

controls.reason: RFC 9309 syntax and semantics are machine-testable, while documentation and access tests can show robots rules are not used for confidentiality.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every robots.txt file conforms to RFC 9309.
No confidential asset relies only on robots.txt for access restriction.

controls.reason: Robots files have exact parser, reachability, monitor, host, and protocol assertions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every relevant host and protocol returns a syntactically valid robots.txt with the approved rule digest.
Active monitors verify robots.txt reachability and digest consistency.

controls.reason: Blocked-resource graphs are observable, but determining which scripts, styles, images, and resources are required for crawler understanding needs semantic rendering judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every resource marked crawler-required is retrievable by the approved crawler identity.

controls.reason: Public nonindexable classifications and supported directives permit exact retrieval and directive-visibility tests.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every public-but-nonindexable resource returns a supported noindex directive retrievable by the intended crawler.

controls.reason: Header directives are inspectable, but where non-HTML resources should be nonindexable requires search-policy context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every non-HTML resource marked nonindexable returns its approved response-header indexing directive.

controls.reason: Protection intent, crawler directives, authentication, deletion, and canonical state can be compared to reject robots-only substitutes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: No resource uses robots.txt as its sole mechanism when its declared intent requires noindex, deletion, authentication, or canonicalization.

controls.reason: Proving no staging, preview, search, filter, cart, account, admin, debug, or internal page is accidentally indexed requires complete discovery and intent knowledge.
Proving sensitive query parameters never enter any public index, analytics, log, sitemap, or link requires complete data classification and all-scope flow coverage.
A deleted-content inventory supplies exact expected statuses and supports deterministic sitemap and internal-link absence checks.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deleted URL returns its declared permanent or temporary removal status.
No deleted URL appears in current sitemaps or internal-link graphs.

controls.reason: Declared maintenance windows and route probes allow exact comparison between temporary-unavailability and success status codes.

deterministic_clauses.statement: During each short maintenance state, affected routes return the approved temporary-unavailability status rather than success.

controls.reason: Missing, blocked, and failed resource scenarios have exact expected non-success statuses and error-body assertions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared missing, blocked, or failed resource scenario returns its expected non-success status rather than a success status with error content.

controls.reason: Failure-mode probes and index directives are testable, but deciding whether fallback content is unintended or misleading requires semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: DNS, TLS, redirect, timeout, and server-failure scenarios do not expose fallback or error responses marked indexable.

controls.reason: Safe crawl bounds and important-content visibility require traffic, capacity, content-value, and discoverability trade-off judgment.
A route grammar and parameter policies can bound faceting, calendars, search, sessions, sorting, and repeated parameter expansion.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every crawl-generating route family has finite parameter cardinality or an approved crawl restriction.
Bounded crawl simulation finds no loop or expansion beyond the approved URL-space limit.

controls.reason: Crawler identity verification is protocol-driven, but classifying scraper or bot abuse separately from legitimate crawling requires behavioral and threat judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every request granted crawler-specific treatment passes the approved identity-verification procedure.

controls.reason: Private media classifications and public-network probes can prove independent access control or absence from public URL space.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every private media or document asset is outside public URL routes or rejects unauthenticated access independently of page directives.

controls.reason: The public test origin and production configuration binding make crawl and indexing control results directly reproducible.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared crawl and indexing control has a current public-network test bound to the deployed production configuration.

controls.reason: Encoding stability and volatile identifiers are analyzable, but human understandability and unnecessary state require content and architecture judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every public URL passes the approved encoding, stability, and volatile-state identifier checks.

controls.reason: Canonical signals are extractable, but determining substantial duplication and the intended canonical page requires editorial and search judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every duplicate cluster in the approved content inventory has one intended canonical URL and consistent declared signals.

controls.reason: Once canonical and locale intent is declared, redirects, links, sitemaps, alternates, and structured data can be compared for exact agreement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each URL has a declared intended canonical and locale target.
Canonical declarations, redirects, internal links, sitemaps, alternate-language links, and structured data match those targets.

controls.reason: Material page difference and motivation to suppress duplicate-content warnings require semantic content and intent judgment.
Redirect status and declared move type are directly comparable, but whether routing is genuinely temporary or permanent requires lifecycle intent judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared permanent move uses a permanent redirect and every declared temporary route uses a temporary redirect.

controls.reason: Chains and loops are deterministic graph facts, but relevance of destinations and essential path or query meaning require semantic application judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The redirect graph contains no loops or disallowed chains and preserves every path or query segment declared essential.
